messages:
Maria: Heads-up — onboarding sample app confuses users. We have REDWOOD_KEY, REDWOOD_API_KEY, and RW_API_KEY all floating around. Which one should sample apps use?

Jason: +1 saw two different env names in our python vs node quickstarts.

Priya: For customer infra it's worse — project scopes leak into key naming. Example: REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme REDWOOD_KEY=acme:sk_live_...

Nate: That's the root problem. We need a single canonical env var and a mapping layer in SDKs.

Maria: Proposal: canonical env var = REDWOOD_API_KEY (global), with REDWOOD_ORG/REDWOOD_PROJECT optional. SDKs should accept legacy names too and warn.

devex-bot: draft design doc: <https://redwood-internal/notes/auth-env-unify> (WIP)

Jason: +1 but also add rotation story: short-lived tokens + refresh endpoint. We can't push long-lived static keys in samples.

Priya: Agreed. Suggest: samples show using ephemeral key retrieval snippet. e.g.

```bash
# get ephemeral token for local dev
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KMS_TOKEN" \
  https://internal-auth/redwood/ephemeral?project=acme
# export REDWOOD_API_KEY from response
```

Nate: SDK change: when REDWOOD_API_KEY absent, fallback order: 1) RW_API_KEY 2) REDWOOD_KEY 3) env var file (.env) 4) system keychain. Emit a single deprecation warning at startup.

Maria: UX ask: make warnings non-verbose in CI. Maybe only log once per process and provide env var RW_SILENCE_DEPRECATIONS.

Priya: Security: ensure we recommend KMS/HSM + short TTL (1h) and show rotation steps in the sample app.

Jason: I'll PR a small helper in each SDK repo: getKey() that implements mapping + refresh. Keep parity across repos.

Maria: sweet. Action items: @Jason write SDK helper PR, @Priya add ephemeral sample to sample-app, @Nate update docs. I'll follow up with draft wording for the canonical env names.

devex-bot: Reminder: weekly infra sync Thu 10am — bring any blockers.
